title: Russia's Sberbank to Launch Crypto Trading Infrastructure by December
dek: Sberbank announced plans to launch a crypto trading platform and digital depository by December 1, 2026, ahead of new Russian regulations taking effect September 1. The infrastructure will process most transactions outside the blockchain and restrict public trading to assets exceeding 5 trillion rubles in market capitalization.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: Sberbank will launch crypto trading infrastructure and a digital depository by December 1, 2026, ahead of Russia's September 1 regulatory framework.
bottom_line: Sberbank's December deadline and the Bank of Russia's multi-tier access model will reveal how Russia intends to balance institutional crypto adoption with retail restrictions. Watch whether the depository processing transactions outside the blockchain proves technically workable and whether qualified investor demand materializes before the July 2027 intermediary requirement kicks in.
body: Sberbank, Russia's largest bank, plans to launch crypto trading infrastructure and a digital depository by December 1, 2026, according to CoinDesk's reporting. The move comes ahead of new Russian crypto regulations taking effect September 1, 2026, and signals a shift toward institutionalized crypto trading in a major economy under international sanctions.

The digital depository will record clients' ownership of cryptocurrency and process most transactions outside the underlying blockchain. Sberbank will operate active wallets for client-initiated deposits, withdrawals and transfers, creating a custodial layer between retail users and on-chain asset settlement.

Russia's regulatory framework imposes strict guardrails on who can trade what. Public exchange trading will be limited to cryptocurrencies with an average market capitalization above 5 trillion rubles (approximately $64 billion) and an average daily volume above 1 trillion rubles (approximately $12.8 billion) over a two-year period. Qualified investors will be able to access a broader range of assets beyond those meeting public trading thresholds. Rules requiring transactions to pass through licensed intermediaries will apply from July 2027. Crypto payments for goods and services inside Russia remain prohibited.

Sberbank has already moved into crypto-linked products. The bank started offering qualified investors structured bonds tied to bitcoin last year and completed a bitcoin-backed lending pilot with miner Intelion Data in December 2025. A 2024 Russian law legalized mining and created an experimental regime for crypto-based cross-border settlements. In 2025, the Bank of Russia widened access by allowing qualified investors to buy crypto-linked financial products and proposed limited direct purchases for retail investors, subject to testing and an annual cap of 300,000 rubles (approximately $3,850) per intermediary.

The Federation Council approved a law regulating cryptocurrency trading through licensed brokers, exchanges, asset managers and depositories, establishing the legal framework within which Sberbank's infrastructure will operate.

The tight restrictions on retail access and the narrow band of tradeable assets suggest Moscow is architecting crypto infrastructure for capital preservation and cross-border settlement rather than broad public adoption. The phased compliance timeline, with September 1 marking the regulatory framework's effective date and July 2027 introducing intermediary requirements, indicates scaffolding is still being built.
